quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
Even over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs can affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving ability. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug — illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that drivers must obey. It tells you that right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: This is the shape and color of a ____ sign.

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle means yield. Slow down to a safe speed and stop if necessary. If you stop, do so at the marked stop line if one exists.

questions.question: A red painted curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas and stay off the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before trying to stop or turn.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers that bicycles may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They make vibrations and noise to warn drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make vibrations and noise to warn drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to wake up drowsy or inattentive drivers. They warn drivers when they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No turns.
No outlet.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. You may see this sign at intersections where oncoming traffic is heavy.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange signs are used in construction and maintenance areas.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment in the work zone.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment in the work zone.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you about workers, slow-moving equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When it is very foggy, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that wet pavement is slippery and dangerous. Slow down because it takes longer to stop on wet roads.

questions.question: You should increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead when you:

options.text: Are following a small passenger vehicle.
Are being tailgated by another driver.
Are driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are being tailgated by another driver.
questions.explanation: When tailgated, create extra space ahead of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that wet roads are slippery. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from the left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Begin to slow down when you see this warning.

questions.question: This symbol is used for:

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it travels slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, work vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It looks orange during the day and red at night.

questions.question: Alcohol first affects your:

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your brain's judgment and skill before it affects other abilities. This makes it unsafe to drive.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your rearview mirror.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you:

options.text: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.
Will always stop at the railroad crossing ahead.
Should stop and wait for a signal before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of an upcoming railroad crossing. Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a crosswalk. Watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: You are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren on and lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop right away in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right and stop before the intersection.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren, keep going through. Then drive to the right and stop. You must always yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using lights or a siren.

questions.question: When you leave an alley or driveway to enter the road, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if you see people on the sidewalk.
Stop before you drive onto the sidewalk.
Expect people on the sidewalk to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before you drive onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot, you must stop before driving onto a sidewalk. People walking and traffic on the road have the right-of-way.

questions.question: A good driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way just because the rules say so. Always look at what is happening around you. If giving up your right-of-way helps prevent a crash, do it.

questions.question: The light is green, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partly enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter until you can drive all the way across.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter until you can drive all the way across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely through before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: Georgia's Implied Consent Law means:

options.text: You must sign that you will not drive after having more than three drinks.
You agree to a test for alcohol in your blood if arrested for drunk or impaired driving.
You allow a blood test if stopped for reckless driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You agree to a test for alcohol in your blood if arrested for drunk or impaired driving.
questions.explanation: Georgia's Implied Consent Law requires you to submit to a test of your blood, breath, urine, or other substances if a police officer asks. The test checks if you are under the influence of alcohol or drugs. If you refuse, your license will be suspended.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: To spot dangers early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your car.
To keep up with other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot dangers early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic. Look for signals from other drivers. Expect cars to merge at on-ramps and be ready for quick changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks entering.
Truck exit only.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep downgrade coming. Check your brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign says U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are going.
Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are going.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus picking up or dropping off children, you must come to a complete stop before reaching the bus. This applies no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should:

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
Merge right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road ahead curves left then right.
The road ahead curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road will curve right first, then left. Slow down to safely navigate the curves.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Stop.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: To see objects in their blind spot when changing lanes, drivers should check:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over their left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over their left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. Turning right here would be unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: From top to bottom, the proper order for traffic lights is:

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Traffic light colors are always arranged from top to bottom as red, yellow, and green. Red is at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom.

questions.question: This white sign means:

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Continue at your regular speed.
Look, listen, and prepare to stop at the crossing if necessary.
Stop at the railroad tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and prepare to stop at the crossing if necessary.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you go.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: You should use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is in your way.
It may help prevent a collision.
Another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only when needed to avoid a collision. Do not use it to tell slow drivers to speed up or get out of your way.

questions.question: When you are merging onto the freeway, you should be driving:

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.
The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When you merge onto a freeway, match the speed of traffic on the freeway.
